title: Advanced reactor licensing timelines
bottleneck: Novel reactor designs, molten salt, sodium fast, high-temperature gas, face licensing pathways built for light-water reactors, requiring years of pre-application engagement before formal review even begins. The NRC's new Part 53 framework aims to be technology-inclusive but is untested, and each first-of-a-kind design still needs custom safety-case development. Licensing costs alone can exceed hundreds of millions of dollars.
why_it_blocks: Licensing risk is financing risk. Investors will not fund construction when the regulatory timeline is measured in uncertain years, so slow licensing directly throttles deployment.
current_state: Several advanced designs are in NRC pre-application or review. Part 53 was finalized but no reactor has been licensed under it yet. Applicants report spending years and tens of millions of dollars in pre-application before the formal review clock even starts.
